labels.label: ex:take_closed_unit_disc

hypotheses.paper: M\S endowed with a hyperbolic metric
hypotheses.note: DEC-81 metric reading: GX.IsHyperbolicMetric — a metric on the (Isom H, H)-surface giving its topology, a length metric (paths of variation arbitrarily close to the distance), locally the Poincare metric read in the charts; it is unique (GX.IsHyperbolicMetric.unique). The Riemannian tensor (curvature -1) is not formalized: no Riemannian surfaces at this pin.

metric completeness of m (IsCuspedHyperbolicMetric.complete); proved equivalent to Thurston-Goldman completeness (GX.IsHyperbolicMetric.completeSpace_iff): <= quotient metric of H (GX.IsHypQuotient), => Hopf-Rinow (geodesic lifting by completeness + mathlib's IsLocalHomeomorph.continuous_lift).

a hyperbolic cusp at every s in S (CuspChart + IsHyperbolicCusp, as in WP-35i); each cusp is proved to have finite area (GX.CuspChart.cusp_finite_area: W_c\{s} is the injective, locally isometric image of the strip {c<Im w, 0<=Re w<1}, whose area dx dy/y^2 is 1/c, GX.volume_cuspStrip). Not built: thick-thin (finite volume => cusps) and the area measure of the whole surface.
M Hausdorff, locally path-connected, first countable, connected; genus not used
S finite carried; 2g-2+s>0 not used (it is the existence condition)

findings: l.1879 'finite volume complete hyperbolic metric': completeness of the metric is exactly Thurston-Goldman completeness of the (Isom H, H)-structure (proved, GX.IsHyperbolicMetric.completeSpace_iff), so the example's 'complete' may be read either way; finite volume is used in the paper's argument only through the cusp shape of the ends (thick-thin), which is the one step not formalized.

Carried over from WP-35i: l.1880 'injective developing map' holds for every developing map; l.1881 the neighbourhoods U ≅ {r<r0} exist arbitrarily small (not every open neighbourhood); l.1882 D(U) is a horodisc together with its centre D(x) on the circle.
questions: ex:take_closed_unit_disc (l.1879), DEC-81: may 'finite volume' be read, for the example, as 'a cusp at every point of S' (the ends of a finite-volume complete hyperbolic surface)? Everything else is now proved metrically (complete hyperbolic metric, its uniqueness, metric completeness <=> developing map a covering, cusps of finite area); the remaining gap is the thick-thin step finite volume => cusps (Margulis lemma / classification of ends), and a global area measure on M\S. Under that reading the row could be closed.

kb_proposals: mathlib's IsLocalHomeomorph.continuous_lift (Topology/Homotopy/Lifting.lean) lifts a whole homotopy through a separated local homeomorphism once each path lifts: the continuity half of every Hopf-Rinow / 'section of a local homeomorphism' argument is free.

Path length = eVariationOn of the path; 'lengths are local' is GX.eVariationOn_eq_of_locally (Lebesgue number + eVariationOn.sum'); it gives uniqueness of length metrics agreeing locally (GX.IsHyperbolicMetric.unique).

A metric on a space that already has a topology: MetricSpace.ofDistTopology (topology definitional); state metric facts with @dist Y m.toDist / @CompleteSpace Y m.toUniformSpace, and transport neighbourhoods by subst on the topology equation (GX.exists_ball_subset_of_topology_eq).
Applying a theorem whose conclusion is a def unfolding to ∀ [inst], ... (IsCompleteHyperbolic) inserts the instance argument eagerly; use @-explicit application to get the Prop itself.
A continuous-induction 'sup' argument on [0,1] in this library: GX.IsDevLocalIsometry.exists_lift_hypGeod (sSup of the times up to which a lift exists; extension step + limit step).

Axioms of the main decls: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound (campaign/WP-40b/Axioms.lean). Name clashes checked against GX/ and scaffold/. The row stays partial/unmarked: finite volume => cusps (thick-thin) and the area measure of the whole surface are not built; if the author accepts 'finite volume' read as the cusp hypothesis (question), GX.take_closed_unit_disc_metric certifies the example in full under DEC-81.
